tickets.summary: Handle stale/expired Snowpipe channels gracefully
tickets.description:
```markdown
**Note:** Much of this code has already been scaffolded out at https://github.com/precisionlender/di-eventstreams

Snowpipe channels can become stale if the continuation token expires or if another client takes over the channel. Implement detection and recovery.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Detect SnowpipeChannelStaleException on append
- Drop and recreate channel automatically
- Reset offset tracking
- No data loss (re-buffer and retry)
- Log warning for observability
- Metrics for channel recreation events
```

tickets.summary: Support multiple consumer instances with partition assignment


tickets.summary: Implement health check endpoints for Kubernetes

tickets.summary: Build .NET client library for Snowpipe Streaming REST API
tickets.description:
```markdown
Much of this code has already been scaffolded out at https://github.com/precisionlender/di-eventstreams

Build a reusable .NET client library for Snowflake's Snowpipe Streaming REST API. No official .NET SDK exists, so this must be built from scratch based on API documentation.

The library should include:
- **Auth/** - JWT generation using RSA key-pair, scoped token exchange with caching and auto-refresh
- **Http/** - REST client for all 6 Snowpipe Streaming API endpoints:
  - GetHostname - Resolve account to streaming endpoint
  - ExchangeToken - Exchange JWT for scoped token
  - OpenChannel - Create streaming channel for a table
  - AppendRows - Write NDJSON rows to channel
  - GetChannelStatus - Check channel health and offset
  - DropChannel - Close channel
- **Streaming/** - High-level client with buffering, auto-flush, and lazy channel opening
- **Models/** - DTOs for API requests/responses and generic row model
- **Configuration/** - Options pattern for DI

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- JWT generation with RSA key-pair authentication
- Token exchange and caching with auto-refresh before expiry
- All 6 Snowpipe Streaming REST endpoints implemented
- High-level streaming client with configurable batch size and flush interval
- Lazy channel opening (open on first flush, not at startup)
- Service collection extensions (AddSnowpipeStreaming())
- NDJSON serialization with snake_case naming
- Handle edge cases (Infinity/NaN values in JSON)
```

tickets.summary: Create comprehensive test suite for the application
tickets.description:
**Focus mainly on getting high coverage set of unit tests!**

Create a separate ticket for integration tests on DataInsights.EventStreams.Consumer (should not block production deployment)

Create a separate ticket for getting integration tests running in Azure DevOps (should not block production deployment)

```markdown
**Note:** Much of this code has already been scaffolded out at https://github.com/precisionlender/di-eventstreams

Create unit and integration tests for the consumer application and Snowflake client library. Unit tests validate handler logic with mocked dependencies, integration tests validate end-to-end flows against real services.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Test configuration via appsettings.Test.json (gitignored)
- Unit tests for event handlers with mocked ISnowpipeStreamingClient
- Unit tests for payload deserialization and tenant ID extraction
- Integration tests for Snowflake client (JWT, token exchange, channel lifecycle, row appending)
- Test batch flushing behavior
- Tests pass against real Snowflake test environment
- CI pipeline runs tests on PR
```

tickets.summary: Flush in-flight batches on application shutdown
tickets.description:
```markdown
**Note:** Much of this code has already been scaffolded out at https://github.com/precisionlender/di-eventstreams

When the application receives a shutdown signal (SIGTERM from Kubernetes), ensure all buffered rows are flushed to Snowflake before exiting. Without this, buffered rows could be lost on shutdown.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Register IHostApplicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping callback
- Call FlushAsync() on all SnowpipeStreamingClient instances
- Set reasonable timeout (e.g., 30 seconds) for flush completion
- Log warning if flush times out
- Test with dotnet run + Ctrl+C
```

tickets.summary: Use Spark for heavy RA copy jobs
tickets.description:
Convert the heavy RA copy jobs (datasets that are generally large like Relationship FS, Loan FS Breakdown, Core Loan Accounts, etc.) to using the new Spark copy runner in <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://qtwo.atlassian.net/browse/DE-2357</custom>.

‌

That was done for just Rel FS and just for Truist DV (it was also a bit rushed to get them over the line). It would be good for this ticket to further test that runner that it syncs properly with DatasetMetadata, copies data over the same as it did with the pandas runner. 

‌

See how little resources we need (1 executor with minimal memory?) to be able to handle large files. For reference, Rel FS for 7d8 in alpha is \~3.7gb and for Truist DV was \~27gb. Truist DV was able to handle that find with the default spark configs, (3 executors with 16gb memory. Most likely overkill).

‌

I don’t think we need to do this for the really small RA files, so we dont have to spin up so many concurrent Spark executors.

‌

It may be worth either using Claude to go through and find clients + copy jobs that meet a certain threshold (for example taking more than 10 minutes?) 

‌

General Steps:

1. Validate the primary Relationships FS for Truist DV (c3563e8a-3e29-45e9-9dad-9e6743126d78) data. See if the CSV output from DatePartition=20260226 (pre Spark) is of the same format as anything after DatePartition=20260312. You can just see if the same primary keys exist and if they have the same data, or if some fields have the same values or date fields are produced the same
2. Look for RA copy job candidates to convert to spark
3. Configure for those clients

tickets.summary: Update Relationship Summary Job to only Download latest date
tickets.description:
**Context**

  
The `relationship_signals_summary` job is currently configured to read `RelationshipSignalsTimeSeries` with `DatesToDownload.ALL_DATES`, but the job logic only uses the most recent run-date data to produce the final summary output.

This creates unnecessary read volume and compute overhead because we download historical partitions that are discarded during transformation.

Target job:  
`ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/relationship/relationship_signals_summary.py`

Current behavior:

* Source metadata uses `DatesToDownload.ALL_DATES`
* Job logic filters down to the latest run-date / latest relationship-level records

Desired behavior:

* Update the job to read only the latest required source data instead of full history
* Preserve the current functional output and schema
* Confirm the change does not affect downstream consumers or expected run-date behavior

**Proposed change**

* Change source metadata for `RelationshipSignalsTimeSeries` from `DatesToDownload.ALL_DATES` to the appropriate latest-only mode, likely `DatesToDownload.LATEST_DATE`
* Validate that any downstream calculations still work correctly with latest-only input
* Remove or update the existing TODO comment once the change is complete

**Acceptance Criteria**

* `relationship_signals_summary` no longer reads full historical `RelationshipSignalsTimeSeries` data
* Output schema and business logic remain unchanged
* Job produces the same expected latest summary results as before

tickets.summary: Node Scaling Observability, Scaling, & Impact
tickets.description:
Currently, our Node pools scale down very conservatively. We scale down 2 pods per minute within a window of `1200` seconds. 

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=2c2e6eba-dfea-4b72-b209-52a371dcdbbf&&collection=&height=256&occurrenceKey=null&width=727&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)
Upon job completion in the morning, this leaves many nodes under-utilized. For many nodes, the `%mem, %cpu < 50%`. 

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=null&id=1b1e0a47-cd14-43b3-a50a-6fd968d6a223&&collection=&height=401&occurrenceKey=null&width=1024&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)
Previously, the scaling policy was too aggressive and cause issues speeding up and slowing down pods. Ticket completion will involve:

1. Creating success metric for “good” scaling policy
2. Creating tracking policy and data analysis for success metric
3. Tuning cluster accordingly
4. Write documentation & project cost savings estimate. Extend this confluence page: <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://qtwo.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DI/pages/1021411340/Pod+Sizing+Node+Packing</custom> 

There is no “perfect” solution. We do want/need to improve.

tickets.summary: LoanAmount doubled for opportunities with conversion loans - using wrong source field
tickets.description:
Opportunities with conversion loans show doubled LoanAmount values (e.g., $4.8MM instead of $2.4MM). **We are currently using the wrong field.** We extract and sum commercialLoanAccounts\[\].amount, but we should be using

  allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount instead.

‌

  **Current** **(Wrong)** **Field:**

  commercialLoanAccounts\[\].amount - extracted from each individual loan account and summed together. This includes both the original loan and its conversion loan, causing duplication.

‌

  **Correct** **Field:**

  allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount - pre-aggregated at the scenario level by PrecisionLender. This field already contains the correct total and does not double-count conversion loans.

‌

  **Files** **to** **Change:**

‌

1. ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/opportunities/pipeline_scenarios_opportunities_history_v1.py

* Add allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount to SCENARIO_COLS

* Remove amount extraction from COMM_LOAN_COLS and MC_COLS

2. ds-jobs/src/datascience_jobs/jobs/data/opportunities/opportunities_helpers.py

* Remove LoanAmount/LoanAmountMC aggregation logic from aggregate_account_array_columns()

* This function currently sums the array of individual loan amounts. Since allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount is already a single pre-aggregated value (not an array), the aggregation logic is no longer needed and would fail if left in

  place.

‌

  **Acceptance Criteria:**

* \[ \] LoanAmount uses allLoansFinancialStatement.loanAmount instead of summed individual accounts

* \[ \] Opportunities with conversion loans show correct (non-doubled) amounts

* \[ \] Unit tests updated
